concerns: The paper's central title and abstract frame the work as a cloud-based system using a Squeeze Vision Transformer, but the actually trained and evaluated pipeline is a standard ImageNet-pretrained ViT-small backbone; the dedicated squeeze-layer local-global fusion module is explicitly stated to be part of the formulated architecture only and not the evaluated model [E31e576869c0657c4-B0045].

The cloud claim is not empirically substantiated: the cloud component was storage only, and no serving latency, throughput, memory, or cost measurements are reported, so the practical implication of cloud/edge-cloud suitability is not established by the evidence [E31e576869c0657c4-B0006, E31e576869c0657c4-B0011, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065].

The evaluation lacks direct comparative baselines under identical splits or setups, repeated runs, or statistical dispersion, leaving the reported accuracy pattern without a controlled reference for the claimed efficiency-accuracy trade-off [E31e576869c0657c4-B0026, E31e576869c0657c4-B0050].
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The contribution is modest, essentially consisting of fine-tuning an off-the-shelf ViT-small model on three legacy datasets. The gap between the formulated squeeze-fusion method and the actually evaluated architecture, combined with the lack of direct baseline comparisons and missing cloud/edge empirical runtime evaluations despite the paper's central title and theme, warrants an uncertain assessment.

evidence.excerpt:
Purpose: This paper presents and evaluates a cloud -oriented facial expression 
recognition (FER) system built on a compact, squeeze -style Vision Transformer, and 
assesses its suitability as an accurate , resource-efficient modelling layer for cloud and 
edge-cloud deployment. 
Design/Methodology/Approach: A pretrained ViT -small-patch16-224 backbone is 
fine-tuned for seven-class facial expression classification (angry, disgust, fear, happy, 
neutral, sad, and surprise). Images from three benchmark datasets (CK+, JAFFE, and 
KDEF) are preprocessed by resizing, converting to grayscale, converting to tensors, 
normalising, and expanding channels. The model is trained with cross-entropy loss and 
the Adam optimiser over ten epochs. Performance is assessed using accuracy, loss, per-
class precision, recall, and F1-score, macro-averaged metrics, and confusion matrices. 
Research

Limitation: Evaluation relies on controlled laboratory datasets and measures 
classification performance offline. Generalisation to in-the-wild data and end -to-end 
cloud-serving latency, throughput, and cost have not yet been tested.  
Findings: The model attains 97.5% accuracy on CK+ (macro F1 of 0.956), 95.0% on 
JAFFE (macro F1 of 0.946), and 86.1% on KDEF (macro F1 of 0.857). Accuracy is 
highest on the tightly controlled CK+ and JAFFE datasets and lower on the more 
heterogeneous KDEF, with Fear and Disgust the most frequently confused expressions 
across all three datasets. 
Practical Implication: The results indicate that compact, squeeze -style vision 
transformers can act as an accurate and computationally efficient modelling layer for 
cloud and edge -cloud FER services. They reduce the computational complexity and 
memory required per inference request, simplifying

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The paper's central title and abstract frame the work as a cloud-based system using a Squeeze Vision Transformer, but the actually trained and evaluated pipeline is a standard ImageNet-pretrained ViT-small backbone; the dedicated squeeze-layer local-global fusion module is explicitly stated to be part of the formulated architecture only and not the evaluated model [E31e576869c0657c4-B0045].

The cloud claim is not empirically substantiated: the cloud component was storage only, and no serving latency, throughput, memory, or cost measurements are reported, so the practical implication of cloud/edge-cloud suitability is not established by the evidence [E31e576869c0657c4-B0006, E31e576869c0657c4-B0011, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065].

The evaluation lacks direct comparative baselines under identical splits or setups, repeated runs, or statistical dispersion, leaving the reported accuracy pattern without a controlled reference for the claimed efficiency-accuracy trade-off [E31e576869c0657c4-B0026, E31e576869c0657c4-B0050].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The final outcome is measured with objective dataset ground-truth labels on held-out test splits, not with a learned or automated surrogate judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Accuracy, macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score computed against ground-truth categorical labels on the held-out 30% test sets [E31e576869c0657c4-B0047, E31e576869c0657c4-B0050].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss with the Adam optimizer over ten epochs on 70% training splits, with the checkpoint selected by highest test accuracy [E31e576869c0657c4-B0046, E31e576869c0657c4-B0047].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding cloud-based deployment and suitability are decoupled from the evidence, as the paper only conducts offline training and testing where the cloud aspect was restricted to cloud-hosted file storage [E31e576869c0657c4-B0011, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065]. The evaluated model is standard ViT-small fine-tuning rather than the novel hybrid SqueezeViT fusion architecture formulated in the methodology section [E31e576869c0657c4-B0045].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation reports standard offline classification metrics (accuracy, macro F1, precision, recall) across 70/30 train/test splits of three standard laboratory datasets [E31e576869c0657c4-B0026, E31e576869c0657c4-B0029, E31e576869c0657c4-B0050]. No comparative baselines are benchmarked under identical splits or setups, no statistical dispersion or repeated runs are provided, and no cloud runtime benchmarks (latency, memory footprint, throughput) are measured [E31e576869c0657c4-B0006, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted using objective ground-truth dataset categorical labels on held-out test splits without reliance on learned or automated surrogate judges.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Accuracy, macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score computed against ground-truth labels on the 30% test sets [E31e576869c0657c4-B0047, E31e576869c0657c4-B0050].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss with the Adam optimizer over 10 epochs on 70% training splits, selecting the checkpoint with the highest test accuracy [E31e576869c0657c4-B0046, E31e576869c0657c4-B0047].

primary.limitations: The authors transparently acknowledge that evaluation is limited to offline testing on small, controlled datasets without testing in-the-wild robustness or real end-to-end cloud latency and throughput [E31e576869c0657c4-B0006, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology describes standard image preprocessing (grayscale conversion, resizing to 224x224, 3-channel replication) and fine-tuning an ImageNet-pretrained ViT-small model using Adam and cross-entropy loss [E31e576869c0657c4-B0029, E31e576869c0657c4-B0043, E31e576869c0657c4-B0046]. However, while the paper outlines a theoretical SqueezeViT architecture with local-global feature fusion, the text explicitly clarifies that the dedicated local-branch fusion module was not part of the trained and evaluated model pipeline [E31e576869c0657c4-B0045].
primary.quality_rationale: The contribution is modest, essentially consisting of fine-tuning an off-the-shelf ViT-small model on three legacy datasets. The gap between the formulated squeeze-fusion method and the actually evaluated architecture, combined with the lack of direct baseline comparisons and missing cloud/edge empirical runtime evaluations despite the paper's central title and theme, warrants an uncertain assessment.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript evaluates fine-tuning a compact ViT-small backbone for seven-class facial expression recognition across three benchmark datasets (CK+, JAFFE, and KDEF), motivated as a computationally efficient layer for cloud storage pipelines [E31e576869c0657c4-B0005, E31e576869c0657c4-B0011, E31e576869c0657c4-B0045].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The contribution is modest, essentially consisting of fine-tuning an off-the-shelf ViT-small model on three legacy datasets. The gap between the formulated squeeze-fusion method and the actually evaluated architecture, combined with the lack of direct baseline comparisons and missing cloud/edge empirical runtime evaluations despite the paper's central title and theme, warrants an uncertain assessment.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently acknowledge that evaluation is limited to offline testing on small, controlled datasets without testing in-the-wild robustness or real end-to-end cloud latency and throughput [E31e576869c0657c4-B0006, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065].

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
